Issue: JDBC statements and result sets are not consistently closed
Eplanation: KenyaEMR opens files/resources in the records room but sometimes doesn't close them after use. If this keeps happening, eventually there may be no resources left for new work.
Evidence: CallableStatement objects passed to EtlAdminJobManager.execute are cleared from tracking but not closed; lock-check Statement and ResultSet objects also remain unclosed
Potential Impact: Database cursor and driver/native-memory retention; connection-pool exhaustion; failures after repeated ETL execution
Recommended Remediation: Use try-with-resources for every Statement, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, and ResultSet

Issue: Complete patient population is loaded and serialized
Eplanation: For some reports, the system tries to bring the entire patient register onto one desk at once, even when it doesn't need all of it. That consumes a lot of memory and can make the application slow or even crash.
Evidence: Both methods call getAllPatients() and place full Patient entities into a JSONObject
Potential Impact: Large heap spikes; long garbage-collection pauses; oversized responses; possible OutOfMemoryError
Recommended Remediation: Remove unused endpoints or return small projections with filtering, pagination, and strict result limits

Issue: Transactions are not explicitly rolled back on failure
Eplanation: If a database operation fails halfway, the system doesn't always properly undo/clean up the unfinished work. This can leave database resources or locks hanging around.
Evidence: Transactions are begun and committed but failure paths rethrow without checking tx.isActive() and rolling back
Potential Impact: Database locks and transaction state may remain until session cleanup; cancellation failures may recover inconsistently
Recommended Remediation: Use Spring transaction management or explicitly roll back every active transaction before propagating failure

Issue: Shared in-memory lock protects REST and legacy UI jobs but not all execution surfaces
Eplanation: There is a mechanism stopping two people from starting the same heavy job, but not every route follows that rule. A scheduled job could therefore run at the same time as a manually triggered job.
Evidence: REST and fragment controllers share AtomicBoolean single-flight coordination; the scheduled task bypasses EtlAdminJobManager
Potential Impact: Scheduled refresh can overlap administrator jobs; separate JVM nodes can also run jobs concurrently
Recommended Remediation: Route the scheduler through the same manager and add a tenant-aware database advisory lock or atomic job-control table

Issue: Multiple DDL and DML procedures run in broad transaction scopes
Eplanation: Some jobs perform too much work before releasing the database. Other activities may have to wait longer while that work completes.
Evidence: Procedure groups execute sequentially before status query and commit; MySQL DDL may implicitly commit
Potential Impact: Long-held connections and locks; undo-log growth; replication lag; unclear partial-failure recovery
Recommended Remediation: Define explicit phase boundaries and validate MySQL transaction semantics for each stored procedure

Issue: Scheduled refresh leaves its CallableStatement open
Eplanation: Some very heavy operations can be triggered in a way normally meant just for retrieving information. They should require a deliberate action so they aren't accidentally triggered.
Evidence: sp_scheduled_updates is prepared and executed without try-with-resources
Potential Impact: Statement resources remain until connection cleanup; repeated runs add pool and driver pressure
Recommended Remediation: Wrap the CallableStatement in try-with-resources and add explicit rollback

Issue: Expensive mutating ETL operations remain GET endpoints
Eplanation: The same ETL processing logic exists in multiple places. So when you fix a problem in one place, you may forget the other copy.
Evidence: recreateTables, refreshTables, recreateDatatoolsTables, recreateDwapiTables, and recreateFacilitywideTables use RequestMethod.GET
Potential Impact: Retries, prefetching, monitoring, or crawlers can trigger unintended ETL jobs
Recommended Remediation: Use authorized POST endpoints with idempotency and concurrency rejection

Issue: Stale-job recovery checks only local Java thread state
Eplanation: KenyaEMR may decide that a job has stopped based on what Java sees, while the database could still be running it. Starting another job could then create overlap.
Evidence: recoverStaleJob can clear the in-memory lock without proving that the database procedure and its locks have ended
Potential Impact: A second ETL job may start while the database is still processing the previous job
Recommended Remediation: Verify database job or advisory-lock ownership before clearing local state

Issue: Statement cancellation has no enforced query or job timeout
Eplanation: If an extraction job gets stuck, there isn't a strong enough “you've taken too long, stop now” mechanism.
Evidence: stopActiveJob calls Statement.cancel but no JDBC query timeout or maximum job runtime is configured
Potential Impact: A driver or stored procedure may ignore cancellation and leave the single-flight lock occupied indefinitely
Recommended Remediation: Add query timeout, lock-wait timeout, maximum runtime, connection/session ID tracking, and a documented forced-stop procedure

Issue: ETL schema is printed and logged repeatedly
Eplanation: The application repeatedly writes information to logs that it doesn't need to keep repeating — basically unnecessary noise.
Evidence: getEtlDatabaseName writes to System.out and the application log on every call
Potential Impact: Unnecessary synchronous output and noisy logs during ETL query construction
Recommended Remediation: Log schema discovery once when the cache is initialized and remove System.out
